name: EmotiVoice
description: NetEase Youdao's prompt-controlled, multi-voice emotional TTS engine (netease-youdao/EmotiVoice). Ships two self-hosted listeners: an OpenAI-compatible FastAPI server (port 8000) exposing POST /v1/audio/speech with no API-key check, and a Streamlit web demo (port 8501). No authentication on either.
auth_notes: No authentication on either service. The FastAPI OpenAI-compatible server (openaiapi.py, uvicorn openaiapi:app on port 8000) performs no API-key check - POST /v1/audio/speech is open with Pydantic-schema-only validation. The Streamlit demo (demo_page.py, port 8501, the Docker-exposed default) has no access control. No token, no basic auth, no rate limiting on either. The endpoint mimics the OpenAI TTS API shape but omits OpenAI's Authorization requirement.

shodan_dorks.rationale: The FastAPI /openapi.json and /docs Swagger expose the /v1/audio/speech path in served content; the OpenAI-compat speech path on port 8000 is the primary body-reachable signal since the FastAPI root is JSON.

The EmotiVoice request schema class SpeechRequest (input, voice, prompt, language, model, response_format, speed) surfaces in the FastAPI /openapi.json schema; a distinctive, near-unique body match for this server.

Conjunctive: the OpenAI-compat speech path plus the EmotiVoice-specific 'prompt' emotion-control field in the openapi schema distinguishes EmotiVoice from generic OpenAI-compatible TTS servers on 8000.

The Streamlit demo (port 8501) runs on TornadoServer with stMain/_stcore markers; the EmotiVoice name is DOM-injected (SPA-blind), so route the Streamlit surface via the Streamlit server fingerprint and confirm identity via a JS-rendering crawler or the co-located :8000 API.

known_vulns: OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/audio/speech with no API-key check - open unauthenticated TTS inference and GPU compute abuse
No rate limiting on the FastAPI endpoint - trivially scripted compute-exhaustion
Streamlit /_stcore/stream WebSocket is an exposed control channel on port 8501
FastAPI /docs and /openapi.json expose the full API schema (including the emotion-prompt field) unauthenticated
GPU required for inference (syq163/emoti-voice image) - unauth access = direct theft of operator GPU capacity
risk_notes: EmotiVoice presents the richest surface of the two-listener designs: an unauthenticated OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/audio/speech that self-documents via FastAPI /openapi.json and /docs. Vectors: (1) Free unauthenticated GPU inference / compute theft - the endpoint mimics OpenAI's TTS shape but drops the API-key requirement, so any client that would call OpenAI can point at an open EmotiVoice instance at zero cost; (2) Emotion/prompt-controlled synthesis abuse - the 'prompt' field drives emotional delivery, raising the fidelity of vishing/deepfake output; (3) Streamlit control-channel exposure via /_stcore/stream on 8501. Shodan visibility is split: the :8000 FastAPI root is JSON (not branded HTML), so harvest via the /openapi.json-reachable /v1/audio/speech and SpeechRequest schema strings rather than a title dork; the :8501 Streamlit app is a JS-rendered SPA whose page_title 'demo page' and bilingual labels ('Speaker ID (说话人)', 'Prompt (开心/悲伤)', 'Synthesize (合成)') are DOM-injected and http.html-blind - route it via the TornadoServer/stMain Streamlit fingerprint and confirm through a JS-rendering crawler or the co-located API.
deployment_notes: ~8.5k stars, not archived (velocity slowed, last push 2024-08-13). Two listeners: FastAPI OpenAI-compatible API on port 8000 (uvicorn openaiapi:app, server header 'uvicorn') and a Streamlit demo on port 8501 (demo_page.py / openaidemo_page.py, server header 'TornadoServer'). Official Docker image syq163/emoti-voice:latest (NVIDIA GPU required). The FastAPI surface is JSON-only at root - use /openapi.json and /docs for identity and the /v1/audio/speech + SpeechRequest schema for dorking; the Streamlit surface is SPA-blind on http.html, so pivot on the Streamlit server fingerprint (TornadoServer, /_stcore/, stMain) and read the app via a browser/Censys crawl. No TLS in the default configuration.
